ToneOptions.Label: Authoritative & Precise
ToneOptions.FullPhrase: Maintain an authoritative, precise, and technically rigorous tone suitable for architects and engineers.

ToneOptions.Label: Solution-Oriented Clarity
ToneOptions.FullPhrase: Adopt a clear, solution-oriented tone, emphasizing functional outcomes and technical implementation details.

ToneOptions.Label: Compliance-Focused Rigor
ToneOptions.FullPhrase: Employ a rigorous, compliance-aware tone, highlighting data integrity, security, and legal defensibility.

ToneOptions.Label: Performance-Driven Detail
ToneOptions.FullPhrase: Use a detailed, performance-centric tone, focusing on latency, scalability, and efficiency metrics.

GoalOptions.Label: Enable Engineering Build
GoalOptions.Text: Empower the engineering team to accurately implement the AI inference layer, ensuring all microservices and RAG components align with architectural specifications. Success means engineers can develop and integrate features with minimal ambiguity, meeting performance and security requirements.

GoalOptions.Label: Validate QA Strategy
GoalOptions.Text: Provide the QA Lead with a comprehensive understanding of the system's expected behavior, edge cases, and performance benchmarks for the AI-driven data minimization and privilege review. This enables the creation of robust test plans that validate accuracy, latency, and compliance.

GoalOptions.Label: Align Architectural Vision
GoalOptions.Text: Ensure all stakeholders, particularly the engineering team, fully grasp the architectural vision for the AI inference layer, including its event-driven nature, multi-tenancy, and sub-200ms p99 latency target. Success is achieved when implementation choices consistently reflect this core vision.

GoalOptions.Label: Facilitate Future Scaling
GoalOptions.Text: Lay a clear technical foundation that enables future scaling and evolution of the AI-driven e-discovery platform. This document should detail design patterns and interfaces that support adding new models or legal corpora without significant architectural refactoring, ensuring long-term adaptability.

CriteriaOptions.Label: Technical Implementation Readiness
Criteria: All microservice interfaces (APIs, event contracts) are fully defined and unambiguous.
Data models for feature store enrichment and AI inference input/output are explicitly detailed.
Performance targets (e.g., sub-200ms p99 latency) are clearly linked to specific architectural components.
Security considerations (e.g., OAuth 2.0/OIDC integration, data isolation) are addressed for each component.

CriteriaOptions.Label: Quality Assurance & Compliance
Criteria: Testable requirements for AI model accuracy (e.g., TAR precision/recall) are specified.
Mechanisms for auditability and explainability of AI inference decisions are outlined.
Data privacy and privilege review compliance requirements (e.g., data minimization) are clearly documented.
Error handling and resilience strategies for the inference layer are defined for QA validation.

CriteriaOptions.Label: Architectural Cohesion & Scalability
Criteria: The document clearly articulates how the RAG, citation verification, and TAR components integrate into a unified AI inference layer.
Scalability considerations for handling increased legal corpora and user load are detailed.
The event-driven architecture is consistently applied and described across relevant services.
Dependencies between microservices and external systems (e.g., feature store) are explicitly mapped.
